_doc: Multi-day arcs (setup, escalation, climax, resolution) run by StorytellerArcs on top of StoryThreads. At most one big arc per household at a time; the town has its own arc slot (scope town). A stage has after:[min,max] days, text, fx (see storyteller_fx.gd), or options (a player choice at the climax; townies take 'auto'). Safety rules: nothing sexual, nothing graphic; the admirer arc ends with police or a resolution.

stages.text: {other} complained about {name}'s hedge, loudly, in front of the street.
{other} has been telling the neighbours stories about {name}.
{other} and {name} are barely speaking. A neighbour offers to sit them both down.

options.label: Sit down and talk
options.text: It was awkward for ten minutes. Then they found they had a lot in common.

options.label: Give as good as you get
options.text: The feud became the talk of the street.

options.label: Rise above it
options.text: {name} stopped rising to it, and eventually {other} ran out of steam.

stages.text: The feud with {other} is over, one way or another.
Someone keeps leaving small gifts at {name}'s door without a name.
{other} has been seen waiting outside the places {name} goes. {name} feels watched.
{other} left a long, intense letter for {name}. It is time to deal with this.

options.label: Go to the police
options.text: The police had a firm word with {other}, who was told to keep away.

options.label: Ask friends to stand with you
options.text: {name}'s friends made it clear {other} should stop.

options.label: Ignore it
options.text: {name} tried to ignore it, but the worry did not go away.

stages.text: {other} has stopped turning up. {name} can breathe again.
Small thefts across {zone} are being put down to one person: {other}.
{other} has been seen with a new crowd and flashing money. Break-ins are up.
The police have a lead on {other}. They need someone who knows the area to speak up.

options.label: Pass on what you know
options.text: Your tip helped. {other} was picked up.

stages.text: {other} is off the streets of {zone}, and things are calmer.
Old letters turned up in a box at {name}'s home. They mention someone called {other}.
{other} got in touch. They say they know something about {name}'s family.
{other} wants to tell {name} the whole story, but it might upset the family.

options.label: Hear the whole story
options.text: It was a surprise, and a kind one. The family is bigger than {name} knew.

options.label: Leave the past alone
options.text: {name} decided the past could stay where it was.

stages.text: The family secret is out, and everyone has learned to live with it.
{other}'s shop on {zone} has fewer customers than it used to.
{other} is behind on the rent and has put up a sign asking customers to stay loyal.
{other}'s shop is close to shutting. A shopper could make a difference.

options.label: Spend 40 coins there
options.text: {other} was moved. Word got around and a few more people came.

stages.text: {other}'s shop on {zone} has closed its doors. It will be missed.
A sickness is spreading on {zone}. People are staying home.
The clinic is full and shelves are bare of medicine.
The council asks households to chip in for the clinic.
The sickness has passed. The town takes a deep breath.
{other} has been spending a lot of time with {name}'s friends. Everyone senses something.
Two people in {name}'s circle both seem to care about {other}. Tempers are short.
Everyone is waiting for {name} to say something.

options.label: Be honest with everyone
options.text: It was hard, but honest. Things calmed down.

stages.text: The triangle sorted itself out in the end.
{other} hasn't been seen on {zone} for a day. Their neighbours are worried.
Posters for {other} are going up. The police are asking for any sighting.
A search is being organised for {other}. Volunteers are welcome.

options.label: Join the search
options.text: {name} spent an afternoon searching with the neighbours.

stages.text: {other} has been found safe and well. They had simply needed to get away for a few days.
